'''Nicolaas Hendrik Kuiper''' ({{IPA|nl|ˈkœypər}}; 28 June 1920 – 12 December 1994) was a Dutch [[mathematician]], known for [[Kuiper's test]] and proving [[Kuiper's theorem]]. He also contributed to the [[Nash embedding theorem]].

Kuiper studied at University of Leiden in 1937-41, and worked as a secondary school teacher of mathematics in [[Dordrecht]] in 1942-47. He completed his [[Ph.D.]] in [[differential geometry]] from the [[University of Leiden]] in 1946 under the supervision of [[Willem van der Woude]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=51483|title=Nicolaas Kuiper - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref> In 1947 he came to the [[United States]] at the invitation of Oscar Veblen, where he stayed at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] for one year as Veblen's assistant, and the second year as member of the IAS, meeting [[Shiing-Shen Chern]], and he also went to the [[University of Michigan]] at Ann Arbor. In February to June 1954, he went for a second time to Ann Arbor where he met [[Raoul Bott]] and his student [[Stephen Smale]]. In 1950 he was appointed professor of mathematics (and statistics) at the [[Wageningen University and Research|Agricultural University of Wageningen]].

In 1957, he was notably one of the six participants to the first [[Mathematische Arbeitstagung|Arbeitstagung]], an informal seminar animated by [[Friedrich Hirzebruch]], which later became very popular among mathematicians; he saw at this occasion [[Alexander Grothendieck]] presenting his first revolutionary works in [[algebraic geometry]].<ref>[[Don Zagier|Zagier, Don]], "[https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/doi/10.1365/s13291-015-0114-1/dmv-FH.pdf Life and Work of Friedrich Hirzebruch]" (PDF), in [[German Mathematical Society|Jahresbericht der Deutschen Mathematiker-Vereinigung]], (2015) '''117''': 93–132 (p. 106).</ref> In 1960 he visited [[Northwestern University]] in Evanston for half a year.

He became professor of pure mathematics at the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1962. In 1969-70 he made a second visit at the Institute for Advanced Study. At his return from [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]], he gave a talk at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] organised in [[Nice]],<ref>{{cite book|author=Kuiper, Nicolaas|chapter=The differential topology of separable Banach manifolds|title=Actes du Congrès international des mathématiciens, 1–10 Septembre 1970, Nice|year=1971|volume=Tome 2|pages=85–90}}</ref> during which he was appointed in the executive committee of the [[International Mathematical Union]] for 1971–1975.<ref>''[https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1970.1/ICM1970.1.ocr.pdf Actes du Congrès International des Mathématiciens, 1970]'' (PDF), publiés sous la direction du Comité d'Organisation du Congrès, Paris, 1971, pp. xiv, xxiv.</ref> He finally served as director of the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] from 1971 until his retirement in 1985, then stayed there as a long-term visitor for six years.<ref name="The IHÉS at Forty">{{cite journal|last=Jackson|first=Allyn|title=The IHÉS at Forty|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199903/ihes-changes.pdf|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|year=1999|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=46|issue=3|pages=329–337}}</ref> In 1990, he was appointed chairman of the program committee of the International Congress of Mathematicians held at [[Kyoto]].<ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1990.1/ICM1990.1.ocr.pdf Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians August 21-29, 1990 Kyoto, Japan, Volume I], (PDF), The Mathematical Society of Japan, Springer-Verlag, 1990, p. xiii.</ref> In 1991, he returned to the Netherlands to live in [[Heteren]], and continued to participate in mathematical colloquia at the [[University of Utrecht]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Banchoff|first=Thomas F.|authorlink=Thomas Banchoff|chapter=Remembering Nicolaas Kuiper [1920–1994]|title=Tight and Taut Submanifolds|chapter-url=http://library.msri.org/books/Book32/files/dedic.pdf|series=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute Publications|year=1997|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|location=Cambridge|mr=1486868|volume=32|pages=xiii-xv|editor1-last=Cecil|editor1-first=Thomas E.|editor2-last=Chern|editor2-first=Shiing-shen|editor2-link=Shiing-Shen Chern|isbn=0-521-62047-3|archive-date=5 June 2014|access-date=20 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140605052949/http://library.msri.org/books/Book32/files/dedic.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
